purpose: Auditable v0.2.2 harness index for backend/frontend replay, refresh, disconnect, restart, permissions, artifacts, channels, image fallback, and Feishu/Lark coverage.

externalBlockers.reason: Contract harnesses prove transport/auth/callable separation and Feishu/Lark capability gating, but real Feishu/IM authorization and channel calls require credentials that are not present in this workspace.

assertions: Durable run events append and replay by request/session cursor.
Permission, artifact, cancellation, and terminal events reduce into RuntimeProjection.
Projection replay is canonical evidence, not frontend-only reconstruction.
Stable SSE completes through one stream without recovery prompts.
Exhausted reconnect applies backend runtime projection after stream loss.
Poll fallback with a request_id consumes backend RuntimeProjection before rendering legacy text, avoiding duplicate bubbles.
Poll fallback refreshes an existing same-request stale bot bubble from backend RuntimeProjection instead of skipping projection.
When EventSource is unavailable, request projection polling renders image-job-only projection and artifacts without recovery prompts.
Unsafe artifacts are disabled while safe rendered content survives refresh/reconnect.
The smoke serves real chat.html plus JSON and text/event-stream endpoints over localhost without browser fetch or EventSource stubs.
Stable actual EventSource streaming completes through one /stream connection and terminal backend RuntimeProjection refresh.
A real local stream loss exhausts 11 EventSource HTTP requests, preserves last_event_id=rn-loss-1 on reconnect URLs, and recovers from request RuntimeProjection.
The primary real-network validation path does not fall back to legacy /api/history and leaves no recovery action UI.
History page 1 and page 2 consume backend runtime projection before legacy history fallback.
Session history projection exposes only page-owned runtime requests, not the whole session delta.
History projection latest_event_id advances the frontend session cursor before the automatic recheck.
The automatic recheck uses after_event_id=200 and renders only the post-cursor request.
A later manual recheck uses after_event_id=210, proving cursor state is retained.
History messages and runtime request overlays with the same request_id do not duplicate user or assistant bubbles.
A forced page 3 projection failure falls back to /api/history exactly once, keeping weak-network fallback explicit and auditable.

commands: $env:PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD='1'; python -m pytest tests/test_ecorex_web_parallel_backend.py -k "terminal_projection_replay_preempts_sidecar_interruption_recovery or sse_reconnect_treats_interrupted_replay_event_as_terminal or sse_replay_gap_is_explicit_when_cursor_is_too_old or stream_response_emits_interrupted_terminal_for_lost_sidecar_run" -q
assertions: Replay gaps are explicit durable recovery states.
Terminal runtime projection wins over sidecar interruption heuristics.
Restart/interrupted stream recovery does not create duplicate assistant turns.

commands: $env:PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD='1'; python -m pytest tests/test_ecorex_web_parallel_backend.py -k "permission_handler_round_trips_mode_and_audit or webchannel_permission_artifact_cancel_are_durable_and_projected or permission_wait_cancel or smart_ask_requires_permission" -q
assertions: Permission mode changes and denials are auditable.
Waiting-permission state is projected and cancellable.
Capability installation policy uses backend permission/audit boundaries.
Image job artifacts are emitted through durable runtime events and public projection.
Service reset can recover status from the event ledger.
Unsafe artifact URLs are disabled and safe local files route through backend file APIs.
The real image-generation skill CLI/stdin entrypoint is exercised, not only imported provider classes.
Text-to-image and edit routes first call gpt-image-2-pro, then fall back only to gpt-image-2 on the same GPT Image compatible route.
The smoke asserts model_fallback is surfaced, edit requests use multipart /images/edits with an image file, and fake API keys do not leak.

commands: $env:PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD='1'; python -m pytest tests/test_ecorex_web_parallel_backend.py -k "image_jobs_api_surfaces_skill_model_fallback_telemetry or image_job_skill_runner_uses_stdin_not_argv or image_jobs_provider_fallback_smoke_harness_contract or token_shaped" -q
assertions: The Web ImageJobs API invokes the real image-generation skill subprocess through ImageJobService, not a dry-run runner.
Generation and edit jobs call GPT Image compatible routes with gpt-image-2-pro first and gpt-image-2 fallback.

Durable image_job.progress events and public RuntimeProjection expose sanitized fallback telemetry without leaking fake API keys, raw provider error messages, or token-shaped hostile telemetry values.

commands: python -m py_compile agent/protocol/image_job_service.py agent/protocol/runtime_projection.py channel/web/web_channel.py skills/image-generation/scripts/generate.py tests/test_ecorex_web_parallel_backend.py
assertions: ImageJobService caches OCR/vision briefs by hashed image input and reuses the internal brief across same-image tasks.
Web ImageJobs dry-run exposes backend-owned ocr progress, cache hit/miss, ocr_ms, and ocr_brief_hash through durable events and RuntimeProjection.
Production Vision OCR is gated by the existing tool permission broker before any Vision.execute call.
OCR provider failures still emit safe backend ocr progress taxonomy without raw provider error leakage.
Raw image URLs, prompts, OCR text, and token-shaped strings do not appear in public image-job events or projection payloads.
A real OpenAI-compatible external provider credential path completes one Web ImageJobs API generation with gpt-image-2-pro and a valid image artifact while writing only redacted provider evidence.

The seven scenarios cover external generation, fake edit fallback, parallel artifact projection, OCR cache reuse, projection recovery after service reset, running-job cancel, and validation failures that write no runtime events.
The smoke asserts durable image_job/artifact events and RuntimeProjection evidence without writing raw API keys, raw base URLs, OCR text, prompts, or fake provider keys to the artifact.
rows.notes: Requires OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_BASE in the invoking PowerShell environment; the checked-in artifact records only credential source and base URL hash.

Secret-bearing channel fields are masked in visible DOM, inputs, and attributes.

Alias requests such as lark-cli map to canonical feishu-lark before prompt/tool execution.
Auth-required Feishu flows force text-only follow-up instead of blind repeated tool calls.
rows.notes: This is contract coverage only. Real external authorization remains blocked by the explicit Feishu/IM credential blocker.

assertions: Scheduler UI consumes backend projection and bounded commands.
Failed mutations still render the returned projection before alerting.
Scheduler execution rechecks permission broker state server-side.
Project and general sessions remain in separate lists after create/send/reload paths.
Composer autosize matches the Web project-session path.
Dragstart is prevented so project/general sessions cannot migrate across ownership domains.
Streaming and final answers use the CowAgent-compatible Markdown-it renderer.
Incomplete raw syntax markers such as lone headings/code fences stay hidden or inert.
Safe links, code headers, symbols, emoji, and raw Markdown copy metadata survive rendering.
Status/tool text has no sweep or light-band animation.
Reduced-motion keeps status text stable and disables only the small dot pulse.
Terminal done/tool-end states remove live animation state.
Message copy, code copy, artifact image copy, and artifact link copy actions write deterministic clipboard payloads.
Sidebar, attach, artifact action, long-answer, and thinking disclosure menus toggle and close correctly.
The aggregate smoke loads the real Web page and asserts no ordinary Run Center text leaks during UI polish interactions.
Ordinary Web UI contains no Run Center labels, selectors, ARIA labels, titles, or buttons.
Runtime diagnostics remain backend/internal rather than visible user navigation.
The smoke checks visible text, DOM HTML, classes, ids, and role/button labels for leaks.
